Playing Mario Party online (alpha)
==================================

Two to four players, each on their own computer with this same release, their own Mario Party (USA) ROM, the same
mods enabled and the same Board Movement and Map Scrolling settings. One player hosts; the others join.

1. Everyone: start MarioPartyRecompiled and pick your ROM with Load ROM the first time.
2. Everyone: choose Online Play in the launcher and type your name.
3. The host: choose Host a Party. Your party opens, with the address to give the others.
4. Each other player: choose Join a Party, type the host's address and choose Connect!. The host gives each player
   their number in the order they join.
5. Everyone chooses Ready? when they're set. Once all are ready, the host chooses Let's Party! and the game begins on
   every computer. Characters and the party's rules are chosen in the game as usual. Each player plays with their own
   first controller (or the keyboard). Leave leaves the party.

The host's address
------------------
The others must be able to reach UDP port 7845 on the host's computer:

- Easiest: everyone joins the same VPN (Radmin VPN, Tailscale or ZeroTier) and the host gives the address the VPN
  shows (the party lists this computer's addresses too).
- Over the internet without a VPN: forward UDP port 7845 on the host's router to the host's computer, and give the
  others the host's public address (a site such as whatismyip.com shows it).
- On the same home network: the host's local address (like 192.168.1.20).

Allow the program through the firewall if your computer asks.

What to expect
--------------
- Everyone plays from the host's save. A guest's own save isn't changed: its session saves to saves/netplay instead.
- The game measures the connection as you play and delays everyone's buttons just enough to cover it, so everyone
  sees the same game: a tenth of a second or so on a VPN. If the connection gets worse the delay goes up at once, and
  it comes back down slowly once things are steady again.
- If a guest leaves (closes the game, or their connection is lost for 5 seconds), everyone waits and the host
  chooses: Computer plays (a computer player takes their place and everyone plays on) or Back to lobby (everyone goes
  back to the party screen, and the host's party resumes where its last scene started).
- A player who left can join again: start the game, choose Join a Party with the host's address and Connect!. This
  works while everyone is waiting and after a computer has taken over. Everyone goes back to the start of the current
  scene together, and the player takes their character back.
- If the host leaves, the party ends for everyone and each game goes back to Online Play, saying why; Resume Party
  brings it back.
- If the games ever play differently ("desynced"), they put themselves back in step on their own: everyone sees a
  "Resyncing" notice and goes back to the start of the current scene. That is a bug: each copy keeps a record of the
  session in its netplay/sessions folder. Please send the newest folder from every player.

If a session ends early
-----------------------
Every computer saves the party at the start of each scene. The host chooses Resume Party (in Online Play), the same
players join again in any order, and the party picks up where its last scene started, each player as the player they
were. Only the players of that party can resume it.

This is an alpha: a resync or a player joining again goes back to the start of the current scene, and the host's port
must be reachable.

host.bat / host.sh and join.bat / join.sh start a session from the command line instead, for testing.
